title: Decisions the tool proposes and only a person accepts
intro: An architecture decision is a file under the repository's adrs section: front matter that satisfies the decision schema over a body carrying the context, the decision and its consequences. Nothing registers it — the source class `adr` in the knowledge sources discovers it over the tracked tree, and list, show, check, the doctrine and MCP all read that one catalogue. What the tool writes is always `proposed`, because acceptance is the person's act.

scenarios.title: A decision exists because its file does
scenarios.explain: One line per decision, in discovery order: the identity, the status, the date it reached it, and the title.

scenarios.title: What check examined
scenarios.explain: A clean result states what it examined, so that a pass over an empty directory cannot look like a pass over the set.

scenarios.title: The status is not the tool's to choose
scenarios.explain: Exit 15 is REFUSED. A tool that can write `accepted` turns its own inference into repository truth, and a reader months later cannot tell which decisions a person actually made.

scenarios.title: Asking for one that does not exist
scenarios.explain: Exit 12 is MISSING_ARTIFACT, and the message names the command that lists what does exist.
